summary: 儿童文学大多由成人创作、选购和研究，商业与新媒体又影响儿童怎样阅读。文章主张听取儿童自己的解释，并按具体作品评判书籍和游戏。
logic: 成人占主导的文学生产

paragraphs.brief: 这个问题的答案是复杂和混乱的，因为该领域存在许多令人困惑的因素。
sentences: Who studies children’s literature and what is it that they study?
谁研究儿童文学，他们研究什么？
The answers to this question are complex and messy, because of the many confounding factors which exist in this field.
这个问题的答案是复杂和混乱的，因为该领域存在许多令人困惑的因素。

paragraphs.brief: 首先，与成人文学不同，儿童文学一般不是由自己的读者撰写的。
sentences: Firstly, unlike literature for adults, children’s literature is not generally written by its own readers.
首先，与成人文学不同，儿童文学一般不是由自己的读者撰写的。
Adults write for children, and thus adult perceptions of what children are and of what they could and should become are woven into the literature.
成人为儿童写作，因此，成人对于儿童是什么以及他们能够和应当成为什么的看法被编织在文学中。

paragraphs.brief: 此外，一些研究儿童文学的人(以及写某些儿童书籍的人)对文学价值的兴趣比它能够教的课少，无论是培养更好的儿童还是为某一课程服务。
sentences: Furthermore, some of those who study children’s literature (and those who write certain kinds of children’s books) are less interested in literary values than in the kinds of lessons it can teach- either in terms of creating better children or in terms of serving a particular curriculum.
此外，一些研究儿童文学的人(以及写某些儿童书籍的人)对文学价值的兴趣比它能够教的课少，无论是培养更好的儿童还是为某一课程服务。
The issue of how a teacher can use a children’s book is often contentious, but even outside the classroom, much material for children is still didactic.
教师如何使用儿童书的问题经常引起争议，但即使不在课堂上，许多儿童材料也仍然是教学材料。

paragraphs.brief: 第三，虽然目前几乎所有的文献都在强有力的商业矩阵中推广，但儿童文献往往特别成为营销举措的对象。
sentences: Thirdly, while almost all literature is currently promoted within a strong commercial matrix, children’s literature is often especially targeted for marketing initiatives.
第三，虽然目前几乎所有的文献都在强有力的商业矩阵中推广，但儿童文献往往特别成为营销举措的对象。
This fact means that readers are often recruited with a message that is negligibly literary and significantly oriented to ideas of consumption.
这一事实表明，读者往往被录用一种令人厌恶的文学信息，并大量面向消费思想。

Daniel Hade (2002) has raised useful questions about whether children’s experience of reading is altered when their books are part of a larger marketing framework involving the movie, the game, and the toy of a popular children’s book.
Daniel Hade(2002年)提出了有用的问题，即当儿童的书是涉及电影、游戏和流行儿童书的玩具的更大营销框架的一部分时，他们的阅读经验是否会改变。
How children perceive and respond to their stories in this new context is an important question.
儿童如何在这一新背景下看待和回应他们的故事是一个重要问题。

paragraphs.brief: 还必须指出，越来越多的新媒体的文本与印刷媒体竞争，引起儿童读者的注意，并为学者创造定义问题。
sentences: It is also important to note that texts in an ever-increasing range of new media compete with print media for the attention of the child reader, and create definitional issues for scholars.
还必须指出，越来越多的新媒体的文本与印刷媒体竞争，引起儿童读者的注意，并为学者创造定义问题。
Does the term literature’ exclusively imply a verbal text?
文学一词是否完全指一种口头文字？
If not, where are the limits?
如果没有，限制在哪里？
Could a literary computer game ever be considered a work of literature?
文学电脑游戏是否可被视为文学作品？
If not, what kind of attention should be paid to it, since children themselves undoubtedly perceive their print literature as part of a broader continuum?
如果不是，那么应该给予什么样的关注，因为儿童自己无疑认为他们的印刷品是更广泛的连续体的一部分？
The internet provides one forum through which children now communicate with each other.
互联网提供了一个论坛，儿童现在可以通过这个论坛相互交流。
(In 2003, the internet search engine Google listed 7,920,000 sites relating to the Harry Potter novels; even allowing for duplication and dead ends, that is a number with revolutionary implications.)
(2003年，互联网搜索引擎Google列出7,920,000个与哈利波特小说有关的网站；

paragraphs.brief: 最后，在经常对儿童文学进行正式研究的高等教育机构中，至少有三个纪律框架(英文、教育和图书)分裂了儿童文学学术研究的重点。
sentences: Finally, in the context of the higher education institutions where the formal study of children’s literature is often located, at least three disciplinary frameworks (English, education, and librarianship) fragment the focus of scholarly study of children’s literature.
最后，在经常对儿童文学进行正式研究的高等教育机构中，至少有三个纪律框架(英文、教育和图书)分裂了儿童文学学术研究的重点。

paragraphs.brief: 如果那些研究阅读的人能够探讨儿童的看法和成人的看法，他们对于阅读性质的认识就会提高。
sentences: How is the value of the imaginative encounter with the work of literature sustained and honored among such a welter of conflicting interests?
如此众多相互冲突的利益，如何维持并尊重富有想象力地接触文学作品的价值？
One route through this maze is to ask the child readers for help.
透过迷宫的一条路就是向儿童读者求助
As David Lewis (2001) has perceptively noted, what children think of reading is not usually the same as what adults think, whether teachers or parents.
正如David Lewis(2001年)敏锐地指出的那样，儿童对阅读的看法通常与成人的看法不同，无论是教师还是家长。
As Lewis points out, children ‘sometimes see more and they often see differently’.
正如刘易斯所指出的，儿童“有时看到更多，而且往往看到不同”。
If those who study reading can explore children’s perceptions as well as those of adults, their understanding of the nature of reading will be enhanced.
如果那些研究阅读的人能够探讨儿童的看法和成人的看法，他们对于阅读性质的认识就会提高。

paragraphs.brief: Lewis在补充指出，探讨儿童的看法通常是出于教育原因：" 更好地了解儿童阅读方式和如何学会阅读是改进教学方法的先决条件，这是事实。
sentences: Lewis makes a further valid point when he adds that exploring children’s perceptions is usually justified for educational reasons: “It is true that a better understanding of how children read and how they learn to read, is a prerequisite to improved approaches to teaching.
Lewis在补充指出，探讨儿童的看法通常是出于教育原因：" 更好地了解儿童阅读方式和如何学会阅读是改进教学方法的先决条件，这是事实。

However, it can also be argued, as Lewis rightly does, that when children’s responses to literature are accessed and interpreted, they frequently lead to an understanding of how picture books appeal to children.
然而，正如刘易斯正确指出的那样，也可以认为，当儿童对文学的反应得到查阅和解释时，它们往往导致理解图片书如何吸引儿童。

paragraphs.brief: 所有阅读描述都存在孤独症的风险：这就是我所读的，所以这是每个人的阅读。
sentences: Young people’s accounts of what and how they read also enable a more sophisticated description of many of the complex processes involved in reading.
年轻人对读什么和读什么的叙述，也使人们能够更详细地描述阅读所涉及的许多复杂过程。
All descriptions of reading runs the risk of solipsism: i.e. this is how I read so this is what reading is for everyone.
所有阅读描述都存在孤独症的风险：这就是我所读的，所以这是每个人的阅读。
Asking other readers how they read, however, reduces that risk.
不过，问其他读者他们读什么书会减少这种风险。

For example, if I am a strong visualizer as I read, I may consider that visualization is a key component of successful reading and I may judge books by their capacity to evoke a vivid visual response.
例如，如果我阅读时是一个强有力的视觉化者，我可能会认为视觉化是成功阅读的一个关键组成部分，我也可以根据书籍能否引起生动的视觉反应来评判书籍。
Other readers, however, may help me to realize that not everyone reads with mental pictures.
但其他读者或许会帮助我认识到，不是每个人都会用精神图片阅读。
Some readers respond to the patterns of the words, ‘hearing’ them inaudibly like a subliminal radio program.
一些读者会听到这些词的模式，像无线电节目一样，无法听到。
Others respond to the patterns of feelings in the story, responding with an emotional connection.
其他人对故事中的情感模式做出回应，反应是情感上的关联。
Talking to competent readers, of all ages, provides a better understanding of reading experiences.
与所有年龄的合格读者交谈，有助于更好地了解阅读经验。

paragraphs.brief: 成人常常认为阅读任何一本书比玩任何类型的数字游戏更值得。
sentences: Children’s insights are even more important when it comes to understanding the significance of print literature as one aspect of literary culture.
在理解印刷品作为文学文化的一个方面的意义时，儿童的洞察力更为重要。
Too often adults assume that reading any book at all is a more worthwhile experience than playing a digital game of any kind.
成人常常认为阅读任何一本书比玩任何类型的数字游戏更值得。
A humbler approach would include asking why the game appeals to the player.
更谦虚的方法包括问为什么游戏吸引了玩家。
Many adults will probably never develop the automatic skills to process a game as readily as they can read a book.
许多成年人可能永远无法开发自动处理游戏的技能因为他们能读到一本书。
This does not indicate that a book is better, but that a particular set of skills is absent.
这并不表示一本书更好，但缺乏一套特定技能。

Non-players must acknowledge that some fictional universes are thus closed to them, and a logical response would be to find someone who can guide them to the pleasures and challenges of the gaming world.
非玩家必须认识到，一些虚构的宇宙因此对他们来说是封闭的，一个合乎逻辑的反应是找到一个能够引导他们了解游戏世界的乐趣和挑战的人。
Games need to be judged individually just as books do, and any evaluative framework needs to take this into account.
运动会需要像书本一样个别地加以评判，任何评价框架都需要考虑到这一点。

items.en: Which of the following best summarises the writer’s argument in the second paragraph?
items.zh: 以下哪一种最能概括作者在第二段中的论点？
correct: Children are portrayed as adults see them.
儿童被描绘成成人看待他们。

items.en: In the third paragraph, what does the writer say is the main interest of some people who study children’s literature?
items.zh: 在第三段中，作者说，一些研究儿童文学的人的主要兴趣是什么？
correct: the instructive nature of children’s books

items.en: The main point of the writer’s argument in the fifth paragraph is to
items.zh: 作者在第五段中的论点主要是：
correct: explore the impact of computers on the boundaries of children’s literature.
探讨计算机对儿童文学界限的影响。

items.en: Children tend to make a clear distinction between print literature and electronic media.
items.zh: 儿童往往对印刷品和电子媒体作出明确区分。
items.why: 孩子把纸质读物看作更广泛媒介连续体的一部分，而不是在印刷文学与电子媒介之间划出鲜明界线。

items.en: The study of children’s literature at higher education institutions is restricted to one subject area.
items.zh: 高等教育机构的儿童文学研究仅限于一个学科领域。
items.why: 原文明确说高等教育中的儿童文学研究至少涉及三个学科框架，直接否定了“局限于单一学科”。

items.en: Exploring children’s perceptions of reading will assist parents to choose suitable books for children.
items.zh: 探讨儿童对阅读的看法将有助于父母选择适合儿童的书本。
items.why: 分析儿童的阅读反应，有助于理解绘本为何吸引他们。作者没有进一步说明这种研究能否帮助家长选书。

items.en: Adults may appreciate the appeal of illustrated stories better, if they have more information on how children read.
items.zh: 成年人如果掌握更多关于儿童阅读方式的信息，可能会更欣赏插图故事的吸引力。
items.why: 当成年人获取并解释儿童对文学作品的反应时，往往能更好地理解绘本吸引儿童的原因，正与题干相符。

items.en: Children should be asked what features they would like digital games to include.
items.zh: 应当问儿童他们希望数字游戏包括哪些特点。
items.why: 作者建议问玩家，游戏为什么吸引他们。询问喜欢现有游戏的原因，与征求将来应加入哪些功能的意见并不相同。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: Young people’s accounts of how they read lead to
items.zh: 年轻人对阅读过程的叙述导致
items.answer: F · a deeper knowledge of the intricacies of reading.
items.solution: 更深入地了解阅读的复杂性。

items.en: The risk of solipsism is reduced by
items.answer: C · discovering the reading techniques used by others.
items.solution: 发现他人使用的阅读技术。

items.en: Strong visualisers judge books on the basis that they are
items.zh: 强大的视觉分析家判断书籍的根据是
items.answer: H · creating a variety of images in their minds.
items.solution: 在他们脑海中创造出各种图像。

items.answer: A · accepting that literature exists in a variety of forms today.
items.solution: 承认文学今天以各种形式存在。

items.en: When adults read a book more easily than they play a digital game, it simply suggests
items.zh: 当成年人阅读一本书比玩数字游戏更容易的时候，它只是暗示
items.answer: E · the lack of some specific abilities.

items.en: What was the writer’s main purpose in writing this article?
items.zh: 作者撰写这篇文章的主要目的何在？
correct: to review the challenges in the field of children’s literature studies and suggest how to proceed
审查儿童文学研究领域的挑战，并就如何开展工作提出建议

pairs: 第 3 段 · 第 1 句
第 7 段 · 第 5 句
points: 作者建议问玩家，游戏为什么吸引他们。询问喜欢现有游戏的原因，与征求将来应加入哪些功能的意见并不相同。
题干问“减少孤独症的风险”。定位句写到“不过，问其他读者他们读什么书会减少这种风险”。
clauses: Thirdly, …, children’s literature is often especially targeted for marketing initiatives.
连接词 while 引出“while almost all literature is currently promoted within a strong commercial matrix”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
“that readers are often recruited with a message that is negligibly literary and significantly oriented to ideas of consumption”补足 means 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 means 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
